paper_type_evidence.quote: We present observations of the central 9 kpc of the Antennae merger (NGC 4038/9) at 55 pc resolution in the CO (2–1) line obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA).
Mosaicked ALMA observations of the central ∼9 kpc of NGC 4038/9 covering the entire disks of the two merging galaxies were obtained in Cycle 6 (see Table A1 for details of the observations).

question.value: How do the cloud-scale molecular gas properties of the Antennae merger (NGC 4038/9) compare to those in nearby spiral galaxies from PHANGS-ALMA and the late-stage merger NGC 3256, and how do they depend on merger stage?

evidence.quote: To extend the sample of mergers, we have observed NGC 4038/9 (Arp 244, “the Antennae”) at ∼100 pc spatial resolution to add it to these comparisons of molecular gas properties.
Given these orbital details, NGC 4038/9 is likely at an earlier merger stage than NGC 3256, and so offers a chance to probe how the molecular gas properties depend on the phase of the merger.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.00272.S (accessed from the ALMA Science portal at almascience.org).
The primary-beam cube from project ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00876.S was retrieved from the JVO portal (http://jvo.nao.ac.jp/portal) operated by the NAOJ.

findings_qualitative.value: In the nuclear region of NGC 4038/9, the velocity dispersion versus surface density trend flattens above ~10^3 M_sun pc^-2, which may indicate a lower CO-to-H2 conversion factor near the nuclei or gas that is far from self-gravitating.

evidence.quote: While a trend between the velocity dispersion and surface density in NGC 4038/9 is obvious up to about 103 M⊙ pc−2, for surface densities above this value there is a flattening of the trend that is most easily seen in the nuclei in Figure 7 (top panel).
An alternative interpretation is that the gas in the nuclei is far from self-gravitating, in which case no correlation between velocity dispersion and surface density would be expected.

claims.hypothesis: Cloud-scale molecular gas in the Antennae merger (NGC 4038/9) has more extreme physical properties than in normal nearby spiral galaxies.
claims.experiment: Measured pixel-by-pixel CO (2-1) surface density, velocity dispersion, peak brightness temperature, virial parameter, and internal turbulent pressure across the central 9 kpc of NGC 4038/9 at 55 to 150 pc resolution and compared mass-weighted distributions to 70 PHANGS-ALMA spiral galaxies.
claims.result: NGC 4038/9 exhibits some of the highest molecular gas surface densities, velocity dispersions, peak brightness temperatures, and internal turbulent pressures, overlapping mainly with the centres of massive barred PHANGS-ALMA galaxies, while its virial parameters are similar to typical PHANGS-ALMA galaxies.
claims.finding: Merging systems like NGC 4038/9 drive molecular gas to higher surface densities, velocity dispersions, temperatures, and pressures than normal galaxy discs, though the gas remains gravitationally bound at a level similar to normal spirals.

evidence.quote: Compared to PHANGS-ALMA galaxies at matched spatial resolution, the molecular gas in the Antennae exhibits some of the highest surface densities, velocity dispersions, peak brightness temperatures, and turbulent pressures. However, the virial parameters in the Antennae are consistent with many of the PHANGS-ALMA galaxies.
Virial parameters measured in NGC 4038/9, while spanning a large range, are much more similar to the PHANGS-ALMA galaxies than any other gas property.

claims.hypothesis: Differences in molecular gas properties between the Antennae (NGC 4038/9) and the LIRG merger NGC 3256 are linked to their different merger stages (second pericentre passage vs. late-stage coalescence).
claims.experiment: Compared mass-weighted distributions and 2D KDEs of cloud-scale gas properties in nuclear and non-nuclear regions of NGC 4038/9 and NGC 3256 at matched spatial resolution (55-120 pc), and interpreted them using galaxy merger simulations (Moreno et al. 2019; He et al. 2023).
claims.result: NGC 3256 has similar surface densities (with slightly lower maximum values) but significantly higher nuclear velocity dispersions, higher system-wide peak brightness temperatures, and median virial parameters more than twice as high as NGC 4038/9.
claims.finding: Later merger stages (coalescence in NGC 3256) likely drive more intense gas inflows and star formation feedback that heat the gas, increase turbulence, and elevate virial parameters to suppress future star formation, whereas NGC 4038/9 has lower virial parameters and may be transitioning into a new burst of star formation.

evidence.quote: NGC 3256 is at a later stage in the merging process than the Antennae, which may result in more intense merger-driven gas flows that could drive up the turbulence in the gas. The high virial parameters in NGC 3256 may indicate that this increased turbulence is suppressing future star formation as NGC 3256 moves out of the starburst phase.
In comparison, the relatively normal virial parameters in the Antennae may imply that it is about to undergo a new burst of star formation.

claims.hypothesis: A single Milky Way CO-to-H2 conversion factor accurately describes all regions of NGC 4038/9, including the nuclei.
claims.experiment: Examined the 2D mass-weighted KDE of velocity dispersion versus molecular gas surface density separately for nuclear (<1 kpc) and non-nuclear (>1 kpc) pixels in NGC 4038/9 using a constant conversion factor.
claims.result: The trend between velocity dispersion and surface density flattens above ~10^3 M_sun pc^-2 specifically in the nuclear sub-sample of NGC 4038/9, unlike the non-nuclear sample or PHANGS-ALMA galaxies with radially varying conversion factors.
claims.finding: Assuming a constant conversion factor is likely an oversimplification; the conversion factor may decrease toward the nuclei of NGC 4038/9 due to higher velocity dispersions and gas temperatures (or the nuclear gas may be far from self-gravitating).

evidence.quote: However, it is likely an oversimplification to assume all regions within NGC 4038/9 truly have the same conversion factor.

While a trend between the velocity dispersion and surface density in NGC 4038/9 is obvious up to about 103 M⊙ pc−2, for surface densities above this value there is a flattening of the trend that is most easily seen in the nuclei in Figure 7 (top panel).

why_this_data.value: Extending the sample of mergers observed at ~100 pc resolution beyond a single LIRG (NGC 3256) to NGC 4038/9 (at an earlier merger stage) with full spatial-scale coverage (12m + 7m + TP) across the central 9 kpc allows probing how cloud-scale molecular gas properties depend on merger phase.

evidence.quote: However, a single merger that happens to be the nearest LIRG cannot be expected to be representative of all merging and starbursting systems. To extend the sample of mergers, we have observed NGC 4038/9 (Arp 244, “the Antennae”) at ∼100 pc spatial resolution to add it to these comparisons of molecular gas properties.

These observations have comparable sensitivity and resolution but are a significant improvement in area coverage (see Figure 1), and image fidelity (covering the full range of spatial scales) over earlier ALMA observations of the Antennae (Whitmore et al. 2014; Sun et al. 2018).

why_this_method.value: Used a modified PHANGS-ALMA imaging pipeline to handle the complex emission morphology and multiple array configurations consistently with PHANGS-ALMA, and adopted the same pixel-based analysis, constant Milky Way conversion factor, and 1 kpc nuclear boundary definition to enable direct, homogeneous comparisons with Sun et al. (2018, 2020) and Brunetti et al. (2021).

evidence.quote: Given the complex morphology of molecular line emission expected in the Antennae at the resolution of our observations, and the number of lines to be imaged, we requested access to an early version of the PHANGS-ALMA imaging pipeline1 for casa (Leroy et al. 2021a).
Using the same conversion factor as Sun et al. (2018) means any differences in the estimated mass surface densities originate from different integrated intensities.

evidence.quote: Scaling this conversion factor to CO (2–1), with the same 𝑅21 we adopted, gives a value of 𝛼CO(2−1) ≈ 10 M⊙ pc−2 (K km s−1)−1. Given the observed spread in the conversion factor within starbursts of factors of ∼3 to 4 (Bolatto et al. 2013), we have opted to simplify comparisons to previous works by simply using the Milky Way value.

limitations_admitted.value: Virial parameter estimates do not account for external pressure confinement (e.g., from stellar surface density or cloud-cloud collisions) that could help bind the gas.

referee_caveats_inferred: Adopting a constant Milky Way alpha_CO and a fixed R_21 = 0.70 across both the quiescent filaments and extreme starbursting overlap/nuclear regions of the Antennae may systematically bias Sigma_mol, alpha_vir, and P_turb.

Beam-averaged pixel statistics at 55-150 pc assume a single spherical cloud fills each beam with an r^-1 density profile, which may break down in crowded merger nuclei and filaments where multiple velocity components or diffuse inter-cloud gas overlap along the line of sight.
